subject: Re: Redwood — Procurement & Commercial Path for Acme (PO vs Card, Marketplace)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acme.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood — Procurement & Commercial Path (follow-up)

Hi Samantha / Carlos,

Thanks again for your time this morning — really appreciate the clear signals on compute needs and expected Q1 spend. Quick recap and a couple of procurement questions so we can map the right commercial path: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Likely initial deployment: hosted API for product team proofs-of-concept, then Dedicated (reserved capacity) for production.
- Target start: late Jan; ramp to ~150k tokens/day in Q2.
- Security/controls: needs SOC2 + KMS integration; you confirmed that’s in scope.

Procurement / commercial questions:
1) Preferred purchase mechanism: card, PO/invoice, or AWS Marketplace private offer?
2) If PO: typical PO terms (net-30/net-45) and whether Acme requires prepay for new vendor onboarding.
3) Any spend threshold that requires VP approval (> $50k/year, etc.)?

If it helps, we can propose three parallel paths:
A) Quick start via card for a small pilot (under $5k) to unblock product testing.
B) AWS Marketplace private offer (if Acme prefers Marketplace procurement).
C) Standard contract + PO for Dedicated reserved capacity with SOW and invoice cadence (prepay options available).

I attached an example pricing summary (Redwood_Dedicated_pricing_2025Q4.pdf) and a draft SOW for the Dedicated path. If you can confirm procurement preference and any constraints (no card allowed, no POs under a certain dollar amount, prepay required), I’ll loop in our contracts and operations to scope the right paperwork.

Next steps suggested:
- You share procurement contact (if different from you) and any standard vendor forms.
- We propose a commercial path based on your preference.

Thanks — I’ll be standing by to coordinate the smallest friction path.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

[Attachment: SOW_draft_v1.docx]

From: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acme.com>, Nancy Zhou <nancy.zhou@acme-legal.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — Procurement & Commercial Path (follow-up)

Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from procurement side: 

- Preferred path: AWS Marketplace private offers are easiest for us because they map to existing billing. However — we have two blockers: (1) security needs to confirm data locality and (2) some business units are restricted from using Marketplace for core customer-facing systems.
- PO vs card: Corporate procurement will not allow long-term vendor relationships on corporate cards. For pilots, product teams sometimes use card, but corporate policy prohibits it for multi-month committed spend.
- Prepay: We don’t usually prepay for SaaS; standard is PO + Net-30. For first-time vendors with > $25k ARR expected in the year, we have a short security review and may require net-0 or prepay for vendor onboarding in exceptional cases (rare).
- Approval thresholds: Anything > $50k annual spend requires VP approval; > $150k requires CFO sign-off.

So we’re not saying no — just that procurement needs the Marketplace pathway evaluated first. If Marketplace isn’t possible, we’ll move to a PO + SOW + Net-30 model and follow our security onboarding.

I’m copying Nancy from legal to confirm if Acme can accept our standard MSA or if redlines are expected. Also copying Carlos (infra lead) for the security/data locality check.

Samantha Li
Sr. Procurement Manager, Acme Corporation
samantha.li@acme.com | +1 617-555-0227

Subject: Fwd: Redwood — Procurement & Commercial Path (acme) — procurement constraints / exception ask

Team — forwarding Acme's procurement note. Key points: Marketplace preferred but may be blocked on data locality; corporate cards disallowed for committed spend; prepay only in rare onboarding cases for >$25k ARR. Approval thresholds: VP >$50k/year; CFO >$150k/year.

Can we outline options we can offer that map cleanly to their constraints? Specific asks: 
- Do we have an AWS Marketplace private offer option ready (or ETA to list)?
- If Marketplace is blocked, can we accept a PO + Net-30 for Dedicated reserved capacity? Any internal policy that blocks invoices < $X or requires prepay?
- If they require prepay for onboarding, can we accommodate a one-time prepay and invoice rest? What are risk/collection implications?

I’d like a short options memo I can send back to Samantha with recommended commercial path and ask for procurement contact + expected timeline.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Li <samantha.li@acme.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@acme.com>, Nancy Zhou <nancy.zhou@acme-legal.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T10:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood — Procurement & Commercial Path (acme) — procurement constraints / exception ask

Marissa / Lauren — quick notes from product/ops perspective: 

1) AWS Marketplace: we do support private offers and can issue a private offer for Acme. ETA to have a formal private offer set up is ~7 business days (legal + marketplace ops). Private offer would preserve their billing via Marketplace and avoid corporate card/PO friction. Data locality: we can provision Dedicated in us-east-1 or us-west-2 (both acceptable to most clients); we’ll need Carlos to confirm his requirements but we can provide region constraints.

2) PO + Net-30: our sales ops can accept PO + Net-30 for Dedicated reserved capacity. For first-time customers with >$25k ARR we typically require completed vendor security questionnaire and signed MSA before provisioning. Prepay exceptions: we can accept prepay, but finance needs to sign off — it’s allowed on a case-by-case basis for onboarding risk mitigation.

3) Short pilot via card: we can carve out a small pilot (<= $5k) billed on card to accelerate product testing while procurement works through Marketplace/PO. This is standard and low-risk.

4) Suggested message back to procurement (short + options):
- Option A (fastest): Pilot via card (<= $5k) to validate integration.
- Option B (Marketplace): Private offer via AWS Marketplace (7 business days to create; no PO needed).
- Option C (PO + SOW): Standard PO + Net-30 for Dedicated with security questionnaire + MSA; if Acme requires prepay for onboarding, finance can evaluate a partial prepay.

I attached the draft SOW and the pricing summary. If we need legal redlines, please send them to legal@redwood.ai and we’ll coordinate.

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: 2025-11-06T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood — Procurement & Commercial Path for Acme (next steps)

Samantha, Carlos, Nancy — thanks for the quick replies and for looping in legal. To keep momentum, here are three clear paths and an ask to help us pick the one that fits Acme’s policy: 

Option 1 — Pilot (fastest, unblock product):
- Card payment by product team, capped at $5k. No PO. Start within 48–72 hours once payment is processed.

Option 2 — AWS Marketplace Private Offer (recommended if procurement prefers Marketplace):
- We’ll create a private offer for Acme (typical turnaround ~7 business days). No PO required; billing via existing Marketplace processes. We can scope regional deployment to satisfy data locality.

Option 3 — PO + SOW (traditional enterprise path):
- Standard MSA + SOW + PO. Net-30 invoicing. If Acme requires a prepay for onboarding, Finance is open to evaluating a partial prepay — please confirm the required amount.

Requested next steps from Acme: 
1) Confirm which option you prefer (1/2/3).
2) If Option 2 or 3: please share your procurement contact and any vendor onboarding checklist or PO template.
3) If Option 3 and prepay is required: please indicate prepay amount or policy so we can route to finance for approval.

We are happy to start the small pilot while procurement completes Marketplace/PO work. If you want, we can set a 15-minute align call with procurement + legal later this week to nail timelines.

DocuSign link for private offer / SOW to follow once we have your path choice: https://www.docusign.com/link/rdw-acme-offer

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142
